comparator.name: Economics and Business Economics (Economie en Bedrijfseconomie)
comparator.sourceNotes: The adopted 2026–27 annual schedule specifies ten 6-EC common first-year subjects. The Economics track has ten 6-EC Year 2 subjects, and Year 3 comprises a 30-EC open minor or exchange period, QRM III, Inclusive Growth and Sustainability, Human Capital (each 6 EC), and a 12-EC Economics thesis. The Business Economics track instead offers Accounting, Finance and Marketing specializations with different Year 2 and 3 requirements, treated as adjacent directions rather than silently mixed into this formal comparator. The annual schedule shows the thesis in two periods, together totaling 12 EC. Years 1–2 are taught in English with Dutch tutorial, expression and answer options; Year 3 is English, which qualifies the registry NLD flag.
components: Open first-semester minor space; programme restrictions on some minors still apply.
QRM III - Introduction to Econometrics for Economics and Finance
Economics track thesis, shown in two periods in the annual schedule.

routeSelection.basis: The generic normalized programme has an Economics track and a Business Economics track with Accounting, Finance or Marketing specialization. Neither overarching track is a clear proxy for the entire degree; Economics is the first track in the 2026–27 official annual schedule, so the neutral official-order rule fixes it before considering UCR offerings. The Business Economics specializations remain candidate related directions.

core: Microeconomics and consumer, firm and market decisions
Macroeconomics, international economic events and policy
Public economics, labour, development, inequality and broad prosperity
Quantitative economics: mathematics, statistics, programming and introductory econometrics
Accounting, finance, marketing and organisational foundations in the shared first year
Economic ethics, sustainable growth and environmental choices
Economic research, writing, thesis and advice to public and private actors
adjacent: Business Economics Finance specialization and banking or investment decisions
Business Economics Marketing specialization and consumer engagement
questions: How do economic policies affect labour markets, inequality and broad prosperity?
How can banks manage risk and remain financially stable?
How do consumers respond to marketing and firm decisions?
Can energy choices such as nuclear power address climate change sustainably?

courses: Business & Economy in the Age of AI
trace: Personal & Professional Development: This course is a first-year requirement and aims to stimulate personal development, namely, being able to actively, consciously and ethically orientate oneself in relation to others and the  — a UCR contribution to this topic with its own scope and credit weight.

Accounting & Corporate Finance: This course describes the most widely accepted accounting theory and practice with an emphasis on using and analyzing the information in financial statements — a UCR contribution to this topic with its own scope and credit weight.
Business & Economy in the Age of AI: This course examines how organizations are structured and evolve over time — a UCR contribution to this topic with its own scope and credit weight.

Transnational Business Law: Businesses and entrepreneurs are confronted with legal complexity not only at the domestic level but particularly across divergent legal systems — a UCR contribution to this topic with its own scope and credit weight.

Money, Banking & Finance: This course develops practical financial decision-making skills through case studies and real-world applications — a UCR contribution to this topic with its own scope and credit weight.
Introduction to Economics: Explore how individuals, firms, and societies make economic decisions — a UCR contribution to this topic with its own scope and credit weight.

International Macroeconomics: Study the economy as a whole through topics such as national income, economic growth, inflation, and unemployment — a UCR contribution to this topic with its own scope and credit weight.
Microeconomics & Behavior: Study how consumers and producers make decisions under scarcity — a UCR contribution to this topic with its own scope and credit weight.

Public Economics: Investigate the role of government in the economy, focusing on how public policy influences efficiency and equity — a UCR contribution to this topic with its own scope and credit weight.
Econometrics: Econometrics supplies tools to analyze data to answer questions of causality and prediction — a UCR contribution to this topic with its own scope and credit weight.

Behavioral Economics: This course integrates insights from psychology into economic theory to better understand how people make decisions — a UCR contribution to this topic with its own scope and credit weight.
Consumer Product Design: You will learn how to function in a ‘real-world’ design and development team for consumer products — a UCR contribution to this topic with its own scope and credit weight.

Marketing & Consumer Engagement: This course unpacks what drives consumer engagement with brands and how marketers build customer trust responsibly — a UCR contribution to this topic with its own scope and credit weight.

Strategy & Digital Transformation: The course explores how companies develop strategies and drive responsible digital transformation amid rapid technology change impacting the economy and society — a UCR contribution to this topic with its own scope and credit weight.
Market Research: See how companies figure out what customers love and what they don’t — a UCR contribution to this topic with its own scope and credit weight.

International Business & Governance: This course examines the institutional, political and cultural forces shaping global businesses — a UCR contribution to this topic with its own scope and credit weight.
Entrepreneurship & Business Foundations: Through experiential learning, students turn their own bold ideas into new ventures — a UCR contribution to this topic with its own scope and credit weight.

Research Methods & Statistics: Research Methods & Statistics gives you a strong foundation in how business management—and social and behavioral sciences—move from mere practices to true fields of scientific study — a UCR contribution to this topic with its own scope and credit weight.

Psychology of Organizations & Leadership: This course offers Liberal Arts and Sciences students a deep dive into the psychological, social, and structural dynamics that shape workplaces — a UCR contribution to this topic with its own scope and credit weight.

Negotiation & Strategic Thinking: How do you get to yes? In this course you will learn how to craft persuasive arguments, deploy the right language, negotiate more effectively, and influence decisions with confidence—whether — a UCR contribution to this topic with its own scope and credit weight.

Logic & Discrete Mathematics: Focuses on mathematics of decision‑making, covering topics in discrete mathematics such as logic, patterns and structures, with applications to computer science and algorithm construction — a UCR contribution to this topic with its own scope and credit weight.
Introduction to Data Science: Develops foundational skills in data visualization, cleaning and manipulation — a UCR contribution to this topic with its own scope and credit weight.
Machine Learning: Covers core machine learning techniques from linear regression to advanced tree‑based methods — a UCR contribution to this topic with its own scope and credit weight.
Introduction to Programming: Introduces programming and computer science — a UCR contribution to this topic with its own scope and credit weight.

Mathematical Methods: Introduces linear algebra (vectors, matrices, eigenvalues) and calculus (limits, differentiation, integration) to construct and solve equations — a UCR contribution to this topic with its own scope and credit weight.

Linear Algebra: Introduces systems of equations, vectors, matrices and linear spaces with emphasis on visual and conceptual understanding — a UCR contribution to this topic with its own scope and credit weight.

Computational & Numerical Methods: Introduces numerical methods such as root‑finding, interpolation, numerical differentiation and integration and solving differential equations — a UCR contribution to this topic with its own scope and credit weight.
Probability & Statistics: Provides a foundation in mathematical statistics — a UCR contribution to this topic with its own scope and credit weight.

Climate Change: Focuses on drivers and impacts of anthropogenic climate change on sea level, ocean acidification, ecology and society — a UCR contribution to this topic with its own scope and credit weight.

Ethics: Explores theories of moral reasoning—virtue ethics, deontology, utilitarianism—and discusses moral knowledge, motivation, responsibility and the relation between happiness and pleasure — a UCR contribution to this topic with its own scope and credit weight.
European Union Politics: Introduces EU politics — a UCR contribution to this topic with its own scope and credit weight.
Peace & Conflict: Introduces Peace & Conflict Studies — a UCR contribution to this topic with its own scope and credit weight.

alternatives.label: Economics, public policy and sustainable prosperity
alternatives.concept: Microeconomic and macroeconomic study, empirical methods and public economics lead into inequality, climate, institutions and welfare. It connects to VU’s Economics track but UCR does not reproduce VU’s specialized economic-policy sequence, research paper and Economics thesis.
alternatives.labelReason: Public Economics, macroeconomics, sustainability and ethical reasoning organize the Economics-track comparison.
progression: Six four-course semesters in Fall 2026–Spring 2029, PPD in Year 1, at least six 300-level courses, verified term offerings and earlier formal prerequisites against the enriched UCR workbook.

alternatives.label: Finance, banking and business governance
alternatives.concept: Retains microeconomics, macroeconomics and quantitative work, then puts banking, corporate finance, business law, markets and firm governance in the foreground. It is a UCR route related to the VU Finance specialization, not a claim of the same professional sequence.
alternatives.labelReason: Money, Banking & Finance, Accounting & Corporate Finance and business law orient the route to financial institutions.
progression: Six four-course semesters in Fall 2026–Spring 2029, PPD in Year 1, at least six 300-level courses, verified term offerings and earlier formal prerequisites against the enriched UCR workbook.
alternatives.distinctness: Four courses change from the closest match: Transnational Business Law, Money, Banking & Finance, Logic & Discrete Mathematics and Linear Algebra replace Public Economics, Climate Change, Ethics and Peace & Conflict. These 30 EC shift policy and climate toward business institutions and quantitative finance.

alternatives.label: Consumer behaviour and marketing strategy
alternatives.concept: Retains economics, statistics and market research, with consumer product design, marketing engagement, organisational psychology and digital strategy as the applied focus. It relates to the VU Marketing specialization without equating UCR’s route to that specialized VU course sequence.
alternatives.labelReason: Marketing & Consumer Engagement, Market Research, Consumer Product Design and Strategy & Digital Transformation make the focus concrete.
progression: Six four-course semesters in Fall 2026–Spring 2029, PPD in Year 1, at least six 300-level courses, verified term offerings and earlier formal prerequisites against the enriched UCR workbook.
alternatives.distinctness: Four courses change from the finance path: Introduction to Programming, Negotiation & Strategic Thinking, Consumer Product Design and Strategy & Digital Transformation replace Logic & Discrete Mathematics, Transnational Business Law, Money, Banking & Finance and Linear Algebra. The 30-EC shift develops consumer and digital strategy.

candidates.label: Marketing specialization, consumer behaviour and innovation

selection.assessment: The closest route follows the formally selected Economics track, with microeconomics, macroeconomics, public economics, methods and sustainability. Finance and Marketing are official Business Economics specializations and each supports a four-course-distinct UCR path with suitable foundations and advanced courses. UCR has only an introductory combined accounting and corporate-finance course, without the dedicated accounting, management accounting and information-systems sequence needed for a distinct Accounting route. The nuclear-power question is one illustrative policy application, not an entire economics programme; the sustainability concern is represented in the closest path. Production stops at three warranted alternatives.

notes.text: The VU Economics track includes successive microeconomics and macroeconomics, development and regional economics, economic policy, environmental and transport economics, a Research Paper and a 12-EC Economics thesis, alongside a 30-EC minor. UCR can combine economic theory, public economics, statistics, econometrics and related business and policy courses, but does not reproduce these full specialist sequences or the required Economics thesis. The official 2026–27 language rule qualifies the registry NLD flag: English instruction with Dutch options in Years 1–2, English in Year 3.
